title: US Housing Market Stronger

image.attribution: United States Geological Survey / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
U. S. home construction rebounded in July, while the latest data show inflation was relatively tame.

Tuesday’s report from the Commerce Department says construction jumped 15.7 percent in July, the strongest showing in eight months. The gains followed a couple of months of declines.

Investors and economists watch the housing market closely because severe problems in this area were a key cause of the recession.

A separate report from the Labor Department says prices rose very slightly (one-tenth of one percent) in July from the previous month.

Rising food prices were largely offset by falling energy costs. In the 12-month period ending in July, U.S. prices rose two percent, which is a slightly lower rate of inflation than recent months.

The U.S. central bank is trying to keep inflation around two percent.

questions.question: What are the two positive aspects about the US economy in the text?
options: A rebound in home construction and low inflation rate
High consumer spending and declining unemployment
Increase in stock market values and high job creation
Growing exports and improvements in international trade
questions.answer: A rebound in home construction and low inflation rate

questions.question: What can you say about the construction sector based on the text?
options: It is experiencing significant declines and uncertainty
It showed robust growth after several months of downturn
It is heavily influenced by international trade agreements
It is primarily driven by government funding and subsidies
questions.answer: It showed robust growth after several months of downturn

questions.question: How much did the prices rise?
options: One-tenth of one percent from last month
Five percent over the last twelve months
questions.answer: One-tenth of one percent from last month
